name: W Toronto
positioning: Toronto's first W Hotel, in the heart of Yorkville, with jewel-toned theatre-inspired rooms, a W Sound Suite studio and rooftop Nikkei dining at TONO
best_for: Travelers who want a lively, design-forward base in Yorkville near Bloor Street shopping and the Royal Ontario Museum
Music lovers and creatives drawn to the Sound Suite and live music

facts.text: W Toronto is in the heart of Yorkville, surrounded by culture, fashion and nightlife.
W Toronto is the city's first W Hotel.
Guest rooms are jewel-toned and theatre-inspired, and rooms and suites have city or courtyard views.
Rooms have sapphire velvet curtains and beds with an ambient underglow.
Bathrooms are open-concept, with terrazzo vanities and illuminated mirrors.
The in-room Mix Bar has recipes, tools and ingredients for making a cocktail.
In the Penthouse Suites, beds are flanked by shimmery tassel curtains.
Bloor Street has Hermès, Chanel and Balenciaga storefronts and Holt Renfrew.
The gym has cardio machines, free weights, a boxing setup and space to stretch.
TONO by Akira Back serves Nikkei cuisine, blending Japanese and Peruvian influences.
Local artists give live music performances in the Living Room.
The Royal Ontario Museum is near the hotel.

highlights.text: The W Sound Suite is a sound studio for artists, musicians and novices.
Taglialatella Gallery is the hotel's local art curator partner, designing the artwork in the hotel and guest rooms.
The Penthouse I Suites are bi-level.
TONO is a rooftop spot with expansive city views.
The Urban Suites on the 11th floor have oversized window walls.

considerations.text: Rooms do not have a work space.
The room setup favors pleasure over productivity.
WhataHotel notes the urban setting may lack traditional hotel tranquility.
